trigger: operator anti-bluff-mandate invocation (§6.N.1.1 first invocation of the day — full hunt)
scope: lava-api-go Go packages disjoint from cycle4 (allowed: internal/discovery, internal/config, internal/version, internal/server, internal/middleware)
procedure: §6.N / Seventh Law clause 5 — mutate production code, run targeted test, record FAIL or SURVIVED=bluff, revert, re-run GREEN

targets.behavior_guaranteed: Code constant must be a positive integer (> 0); a zero or negative value would signal an untagged or misconfigured release binary
targets.mutation_rationale: Code = 0 is the zero value — would slip through if the test only checked Code != 2332 (an anti-pattern) rather than Code > 0
targets.verbatim_fail_message:
version_test.go:18: Code = 0, want positive
--- FAIL: TestCodeIsPositive (0.00s)

targets.behavior_guaranteed: firstError() returns the FIRST non-nil concrete error from gin.Errors, not the last; mis-labelling a Firebase non-fatal with the wrong error identity would make telemetry misleading
targets.mutation: Changed early-return `return e.Err` inside loop to collect `last = e.Err` and `return last` after loop — turning first-wins into last-wins
targets.mutation_rationale: The last-wins variant produces the same result for single-error slices (the most common case) and for all-nil slices; only the multi-error case distinguishes them
targets.verbatim_fail_message:
first_error_test.go:25: firstError: got boom-2, want first boom-1
--- FAIL: TestFirstError_ReturnsFirstConcrete (0.00s)

targets.behavior_guaranteed: Announce() fills port=0 with DefaultPort (8443) before passing to upstream; passing port=0 raw causes upstream validation to reject with 'Port 0 out of range (1..65535)'
targets.mutation: Changed `if port == 0 {` to `if port < 0 {` — so port=0 is no longer treated as 'use default', flowing through to upstream which rejects it; simultaneously port=-1 is now incorrectly filled with DefaultPort, silencing the expected out-of-range error
targets.mutation_rationale: The off-by-one in the fill guard (`< 0` vs `== 0`) is a realistic typo that passes compilation but breaks both the positive default-fill path and the negative-port rejection path
targets.verbatim_fail_message:
announce_unit_test.go:68: Announce with default instance+port: mdns: Announcement.Port 0 out of range (1..65535)
--- FAIL: TestAnnounce_DefaultFillThenRegister (0.00s)
announce_unit_test.go:50: Announce with port=-1 returned nil error; expected range refusal
--- FAIL: TestAnnounce_RejectsOutOfRangePort (0.00s)

notes: All three mutations targeted the production code path the test claims to cover (not unrelated branches). Each revert confirmed by re-running the test suite to GREEN. No files were left mutated. No version bumps, commits, or distributes performed.
